docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
I am Justice Chukwuemeka, an Associate IT Professional participating in the University of Wisconsin-Madison Information Technology Job ROtation Program.

My professional interests center on systems administration, cloud infrastructure, high-throughput computing, automation, and the operational practices that keep large computing envrionments reliable and scalable.

Through the rotation program, I have had the opportunity to work across multiple areas of information technology, including held desk operations, cloud services, and high-performance research computing. These experiences have allowed me to develop both technical depth and an understanding of how technology supports users, researchers, and institutional operations.

docs.title: Program Structure
docs.text:
The Information Technology Job Rotation Program is a two-year professional development program that provides participants with experience across four different IT organizations.

Each rotation lasts approximately six months and exposes participants to new technologies, operational environments, and busines needs.

The program is designed to develop well-rounded technology professionals by providing experience across multiple disciplines rather than a single specialization.

docs.title: Migrating Research Data While Resolving Storage Constraints
Overview
docs.text:
During a data migration effort, a researcher needed to transfer data between storage locations. The migration process encountered storage limitations that prevented a straightforward transfer.

The task requied troubleshooting filesystem behavior, identifying the root cause, and selecting an alternative migration approach.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Linux
  • rsync
  • Research Storage Systems
  • Large Dataset
  • Command-Line Interface

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A researcher needed to transfer a large dataset between storage locations.

The transfer repeatedly failed with disk quoate and storage-capacity related errors despite the destination filesystem appearing to have available space.

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text:
I examined the rsync output and verified destination storage characteristics.

To understand the failure, I:

  • Reviewed erro messages generated by rsync
  • Compared reported quota limits against the requested transfer size
  • Verified filesystem usage and available capacity
  • Considered the difference between overall filesystem space and user-specific quoata allocations

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
• Confirmed the failure was quoate related
  • Worked with a research facilitator to increase the researcher's quoata limits
  • Validated available storage before restarting the transfer
  • Re-ran the migration using rsync
  • Monitored transfer progress and verified completion

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: The migration completed successfully once the destination storage constraints were addressed. And the researcher was able to continue working with the required data.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text: I understood storage systems, filesystem constraints, and the importance of validating assumptions before large-scale data transfers.

docs.title: Recoving a ChromeOS Device from Cryptohome Failure
Overview
docs.text: A ChromeOS device experienced Linux terminal failures caused by operating system and cryptohome issues.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• ChromeOS
  • Crostini Linux
  • Student Laptop

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The Linux development environment would not launch and stand user functionality was impacted.

docs.title: Actions Take
docs.text:
• Performed operating system updates
  • Attempted standard recovery procedures
  • Evaluated user data implications
  • Confirmed recovery options from vendor documentation
  • Executed a Powerwash reset

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: The device was restored to a healthy state and returned to service. The client was able to launch linux within their crostini vm.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text: This case taught me how to balance technical troubleshooting with data preservation and user impact consideration. It is essential to figure out how to preserver client's data before making any changes to their system.

docs.title: Resolving an Academic Python Environment Configuration Issue
Overview
docs.text: A student was unable to complete coursework because the required Python environment would not run successfully on their system.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Python
  • Anaconda / Conda
  • Mac laptop

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: A student's coursework requirements required a specific Python version and module set that differed from the student's existing environment.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
• Identified version incompatibilities
  • Updated the Conda environment
  • Installed the required Python version
  • Resolved missing package dependencies using cli work
  • Verified successful execution after remediation

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: The environment was successfully rebuilt and aligned with the student's course requirements. The student was able to continue coursework without escalation to a specialized support team, which would have take much longer.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text: This issue highlighted the importance of dependency management and environment consistency when supporting academic computing workfflows. And also the importance of rereading original instructions and not blindly trusting a client's perceived problem.

docs.title: Service Account Governance for Student Organization
Overview
docs.text: A registed student organization requested for a mechanism for shared communication and website presence.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM).
  • Student organization services.
  • University account governance policies.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The organization required shared access to communication and online resources. Using a personal NetID would create ownership, continuity, and security concers if leadership changed over time.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
• Identified service accounts as the appropriate solution.
  • Evaluated the request against identity management best practices.
  • Reviewed applicable institutional guidance.
  • Routed the request through the appropriate process for implementation.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: While my actions did not directly resolve the client's problem, it steered the student organization toward the appropriate team that would later implement their request. I believe the service account solution was aligned with institutional security standards and reduced long-term administrative risk associated with personnel turnover.

docs.title: Key Takeawys
docs.text: This experience helped me reinforce the imprtance of undeerstanding not only technical solutions, but als the governance and security principles that guide them.

docs.title: Researching Security Governance for AI Services
Overview
docs.text: As cloud providers rapidly expand their AI offerings, organizations and teams faced new governance and security challenges. During this project, I conducted research into AI-related cloud services and contributed internal guidance focused on secure and responsible adoption.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Amazon Bedrock
  • Amazon SageMaker AI
  • Google AI Services
  • Security Best Practices

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The Cloud team needed a clearer guidance regarding the capabilities, support boundaries, and security considerations associated with cloud-based AI services.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
I performed research across AWS and Google AI offerings to better understand service capabilities, governance requirements, and associated security risks. I also collaborated with team members to clarify service ownership and support responsibilites across the Cloud team and PCS.

Actions I took: - Researched GOogle and AWS AI offerings - Documented service information for internal team use - Investigated AWS AI services and related governance concerns - Developed an internal AI security best-practices guide - Documented recommended guardrails and governance considerations for AI workloads

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: The resulting documented guidance provided team members with a reference framework for evaluating AI-related cloud services and supporting secure adoption practices. This project also improved unit-level awareness of AI governance considerations.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text: The number of AI service offerings keeps growing and it is critical teams maintain a good security posture before adopting these services.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The AWS Innovation Sandbox (ISB) project was designed to provide researchers and faculty with a secure cloud environment for experimentation while maintaining governance and operational controls. During my rotation, I contributed to discovery activities, infrastructure planning, and deployment workflows supporting the development of the solution.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Amazon Web Services (AWS)
  • Terraform
  • Git
  • GitLab
  • VScode
  • AWS Control Tower
  • Research Computing Stakeholders

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Researchers required a cloud environment that enabled innovation and experimentation while adhering to institutional governance and security requirements.

The challenge was balancing flexibility for end users with the controls necessary to safely manage their cloud resources.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
• Participated in the project discovery and requirements gathering
  • Supported Infrastructure-as-Code workflows using Terraform
  • Contributed to Git and GitLab-based deployment processess
  • Assisted with deployment activities in an ITE environment
  • Documented project milestones and technical roadblocks
  • Captured lessons learned surrounding AWS Control Tower constraints and template limitations

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
There were multiple technical roadblocks in this project. The biggest is that AWS do not currently expose an API endpoint for terraform for creating a SAML 2.0 application used for managing the cloud sandbox accounts.

Aside from these technical roadblocks, much of the project progressed with a clearer understanding of architectural limitations affecting the implementation.

Most of the ground work for this project was completed during my time with the cloud team. Post rotation, I followed up with them and got confirmatin of a complete proof of concept work.

docs.title: Key Taakeaways
docs.text:
This project provided hands-on exposure to cloud architecture, infrastructure-as-Code practices, stakeholder discovery, vendor relations, and the challenges of designing governed cloud envrionments.

The biggest learning moment for me was the multiple meetings conducted with the vendor to clearly define the capabilities of the ISB solution. AWS assumed we will use their cloud technologies to implement the ISB, however, we are a 100% terraform environment and that caused some architectural headaches.

With this project, I learned that a proposed solution is not always as straightforward as the stakeholders and vendors might expect. There are a multitude of considerations such as identity, compute, and governance that must respect institutional requirements.

docs.title: Enhancing a Cloud Security Assessment Framework
Overview
docs.text: Cloud projects frequently involve varying levels of security risk depending on their architecture, data handling practices, and access management design. As part of a broader security initiative, I contributed research and assessment development efforts aimed at improving cloud project risk evaluations.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Multi-Cloud
  • CIS Benchmarks
  • NIST 800-53
  • Cloud Security Alliance Cloud Controls Matrix (CSA CCM)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The cloud team sought to strength its ability to evaluate customer cloud environments and identify security risks early in the project lifecycle.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
I worked closely with the team's cloud security analyst to research industry security frameworks and examine how their controls could be incorporated into cloud assessment activities.

Some actions I performed: - Researched CIS Benchmarks - Evaluated NIST 800-53 controls - Reviewed CSA Cloud Controls Matrix guidance - Compared security recommendations across multiple frameworks - Developed assessment questions focused on: - Data storage and protection - Identity and access management - Resource governance - Network access

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: This security initiative resulted in a draft question framework to strengthen security reviews and support more consistent project assessments. These ten questions provided a foundation for more structured cloud risk evaluations and encouraged earlier security discussions with stakeholders for any cloud-related projects.

docs.text:

  • Risk Management
  • Cloud Governance
  • Security Frameworks
  • Compliance Research
  • Technical Ananlysis

docs.title: Automating Jira Workflows to Improve Team Operations
Overview
docs.text: Operational ticket management often involves repetitive administrative tasks that consume time and introduce opportunities for inconsistency. To improve efficiency, I designed and implemented several Jira automations to streamline team workflows.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Jira Cloud
  • Agile Operations
  • Team Service Management Processes
  • Regular Expressions (Regex)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The team relied on manual actions to manage portions of the ticket lifecycle which created administrative overhead and reduced time available for technical work.

docs.title: Actions Taken
docs.text:
• Analyzed the Cloud team ticket workflow
  • Identified automation opportunities
  • Designed 7 custom Jira automation rules
  • Implemented all seven automations
  • Tested the automation behavior and expected outcome

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: The automation rules were successfully integrated into the team's workflow and significantly reduced the need for routine manual ticket management activities. One of the more visible outcome was the cleanup of over 500+ ticket alert ticket queue clogging up space.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text: This project showed me the benenfits of automating routine taks that can be time consuming and energy draining. Automation is a force multiplier, and even small improvements can significantly improve operational efficiency.

docs.title: Improving Knowledge Base Accessibility Through a Large-Scale Documentation Audit
Overview
docs.text:
Documentation is only valuable when it is accessible and usable by its intended audience. During my Public Cloud Team rotation, I conducted a large-scale effort to review and improve the accessibility of the team's knowledge base documentation.

The peoject involved auditing approximately 160 technical documents and remediating accessibility issues to improved usability and compliance with accessibility standards.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• Knowledge Base Documentation Software
  • Technical Writing
  • Documentation Governance
  • Accessibility Standards Reference

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Over time, technical documentation had ben created by multiple contributors with varying levels of accessibility awareness.

As a result, documentation quality and accessibility compliance varied across the knowledge base. This created potential barriers for users who relied on assistive technologies.

docs.title: Action Taken
docs.text:
I reviewed existing documentation to identify common accessibility issues and areas requiring remediation. The audit focused on document structure, consistent formatting, accessibility compliance, and overall usability.

Exact actions I took included: - Audited approximately 160 knowledge base documents - Corrected accessbility deficiencies - Standardized documentation where appropriate - Presented my work to the team during a standup meeting - Documented a reference framework for making future documents accessible from the beginning.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
This project improved the quality and usability of the Cloud team's technical documentation used by both customers and team members.

In addition to improving accessibility compliance, it helped establish a more maintainable and professional documentation environment.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
Effective IT operations extend beyonf infrastructure and systems. High-quality documentation is an essential operational asset that improves knowledge sharing, onboarding, support efficiecny, and long-term maintainability.

This experience reinforced the importance of accessibility as a core component of user experience and service delivery.
